gen-fs-styro-gf-krub: Retro and commanding, Styro crowds its letters shoulder to shoulder. Where Styro is best at crowded, forceful punch, Krub is best at quiet, tall-lettered text with curves that stay open.
gen-fs-styro-gf-lexend: Approachable describes Lexend, whose curves stay generously open. Styro hits hard up top with crowded retro letters, then Lexend lets the eye rest on oversized lowercase and uniform strokes.
gen-fs-styro-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga sets flat, single-weight letters with generous tracking. Styro keeps its crowded heading letters tight, while paragraphs in Lexend Giga would drift along open and level, each word given its own space.
gen-fs-styro-gf-lexend-peta: Crowded retro up top, signage-plain below: Styro over Lexend Peta. Big x-height and curves that never thin out would keep paragraphs feeling open and unhurried after the heading's squeeze.
gen-fs-styro-gf-liter: Liter reads upright and uniform, with no stroke contrast and wide mouths on round forms, a sharp turn from Styro. Sustained text would feel modern and unfussy beneath that retro heading.
gen-fs-styro-gf-martel-sans: Retro crowding above, generous openings below. What stands out is how Styro packs its letters shut while Martel Sans leaves every curve plainly open beneath a high mean line.
gen-fs-styro-gf-matangi: Styro hits retro and commanding, letters crammed shoulder to shoulder. Where Styro is best at crowded, forceful punch, Matangi is best at hefty lowercase with rounded letters left open.
gen-fs-styro-gf-maven-pro: Maven Pro keeps its line thickness gentle and its c open. Styro supplies the retro shove in the heading, and Maven Pro follows with a high-waisted lowercase that lets the page breathe.
gen-fs-styro-gf-montserrat-underline: Professional is the first word for Montserrat Underline, whose bowls hold one stroke width and whose lowercase looks oversized. Beside Styro, whose letters crowd, running text would feel spacious and easygoing.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Noto Kufi Arabic reads clean and modern, with an open gap in the c and capitals sitting just above lowercase. Under the tight Styro heading, extended reading would feel light and unforced.
